t: Listen to a talk in an Earth science class.
You may have heard the word supervolcano in the news.
The term refers to a volcano capable of an eruption that throws out more than one thousand cubic kilometers of material.
That's thousands of times larger than a typical eruption.
Now, when people imagine the danger, they usually picture rivers of lava.
But lava moves slowly and only affects the area near the volcano.
The primary danger from a supereruption is actually ash.
Ash can spread across an entire continent, collapse roofs, ruin crops, and block sunlight long enough to cool the global climate for several years.
